newsitem.title: USA: Allegheny says stainless prices could firm in '97.
newsitem.headline: Allegheny says stainless prices could firm in '97.

text.p: Flat-rolled stainless steel prices, which fell in 1996, may stabilize and possibly firm in 1997, said William P. Rutledge, president and chief executive officer of Allegheny Teledyne Inc.

"I'm guardedly optimistic (about stainless prices this year,") Rutledge told Reuters in a brief phone interview. "We may see some stability, if not a tendency toward firming, in European (prices), which will have a collateral effect on domestic pricing."
Despite strong demand, prices for commodity grades of flat-rolled stainless steel fell in excess of 25 percent last year from 1995 levels due to downward pressure from imports.
Weak prices overseas caused foreign producers to export steel to the more lucrative U.S. market, creating oversupply.

"We have a (five percent) price hike scheduled for March and so far other domestic producers have indicated a similar (price hike) at that time," Rutledge said, adding, "We've never seen a cycle where demand continued to be quite robust but where prices have had a severe downturn. It's unusual."

Allegheny Teledyne is the nation's largest producer of flat-rolled stainless steel. The company on Wednesday posted fourth quarter earnings of $0.30 per share versus $0.28 per share in the year-earlier period.
The '95 per-share amount is a pro forma number. Pittsburgh-based Allegheny Ludlum Corp acquired Los-Angeles based Teledyne Inc in a stock transaction last summer to form Allegheny Teledyne.
Shares of Allegheny Teledyne were up 1/8 to 21-5/8 in late-day trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
Rutledge said markets were strong last year for all four of the company's business segments -- specialty metals, aerospace and electronics, industrial, and consumer.
"The markets served by our respective segments are showing continued strength and I'm optimistic about '97," he said.
